content.short: The Graph is a decentralized protocol for querying and indexing data from blockchains.
content.description: The Graph is a decentralized protocol for querying and indexing data from blockchains. It helps developers save time and resources by removing the need to run dedicated servers or carry out lengthy data-processing tasks, instead indexing and querying data from NEAR and EVM blockchains. Users can access liquidity data from published subgraph services such as Sushi or Messari. Developers can create, publish, and distribute subgraphs to simplify interchain data queries for applications.

resources.title: What "Verifiable" Actually Means for Blockchain Data
resources.tldr: Breaks down 1-of-N trust models, consensus and cryptographic verification as separate things, because they get used interchangeably and they guarantee very different amounts.

resources.title: Subgraphs or Substreams: Which Blockchain Data Solution Should You Choose?
resources.tldr: Subgraphs give structured queryable data for user-facing apps; substreams push high-throughput pipelines. Picks apart which workload each is genuinely built for.

resources.title: GraphTally: How The Graph Solved Micropayments for the Machine Economy
resources.tldr: Pay-per-request billing is being treated as new, but The Graph has settled micropayments this way in production since early 2025. Worth reading for the operational lessons rather than the concept.
